soundness_flags.label: ass:observed-activation
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited root-control paper explicitly defines controls as observed roots, so it cannot support the tag claiming observed activation while allowing endogenous controls; retag this as novel and justify the empirical/modeling regime.

soundness_flags.label: ass:strict-cpt-positivity
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited CSI paper assumes positivity of the observed distribution, not strict positivity of every primitive latent-CPT entry; supply a source for the stronger condition or weaken and prove the required denominator support.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 3
soundness_flags.one_line: Nonidentification follows immediately from the certificate definition already requiring a same-observed-law, unequal-query model pair; define an independently checkable syntactic certificate and prove its global-pair implication instead.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 4
soundness_flags.one_line: The binary singleton sink and its sink property are not assumptions on Y or G, while the affine slice and p-vector depend on both; state that restricted slice explicitly and include the affine intercept.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 9
soundness_flags.one_line: Neither claimed example specifies CPT tables or Pobs, although procedure acceptance and the 3/200 gap require a concrete positive certificate/model pair; the reference-context bow is likewise not formally specified.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 10
soundness_flags.one_line: B(s) is called a displayed explicit product, but neither its factors nor the enumeration/bit-cost model are defined, so the asserted effective bound is not yet a determinate mathematical function.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 3, end of Section 2; p. 8, Theorems 5–6
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes a positive distribution over V, proves Algorithm 1 terminating and sound in Theorem 5, and states in Theorem 6 that contextwise identification need not imply CSI identification.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 3, Definition 3; pp. 5–6, Theorem 1 and Corollary 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Definition 3 requires C to be a subset of observed roots; Theorem 1 gives the maximal-regular contextwise iff reduction and Corollary 2 makes the resulting procedure sound and complete.

The published proceedings paper is Chen–Darwiche, UAI 2026, pp. 1181–1199; its abstract establishes state-based versus variable-based identifiability with CSI as additional knowledge and describes an identification approach. The linked primary PDF could not be fetched for theorem-number verification.

The paper proves a sound-and-complete c-gID algorithm under explicit positivity for conditional generalized identification from observational/interventional Q[S] inputs, rather than CSI-constrained identification.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Retag endogenous observed activation as a novel condition, give a concrete application/model class where it arises, and replace the unsupported CPT-positivity citation with either a matching source or a precisely weaker support condition.

Replace the current certificate-soundness restatement with a finite syntactic verifier input whose row-equality, positivity, observational-fiber, and nonzero-contraction checks are proved sufficient for global nonidentification.
Specify full rational CPT tables and observed tables for both Proposition 9 examples, then show the exact 3/200 contraction and the failed gluing check mechanically from those tables.
Give B(s) as an actual closed combinatorial expression with a precise trace/state encoding and exact-arithmetic bit-cost convention; then state a parameterized bound in row-quotient and trace width.
